properties.decision:
PROPOSED as a proof of concept, Anthony 2026-07-27. ⭐ EXECUTED 2026-08-06 at his instruction ("let's trial this out"), after being parked for ten days — and with flo2 SUBSTITUTED FOR STORYFLOW, because storyflow's adopt was never finished while flo2 is actively developed, has a live one-directional dependency on reflow2, has its own graph on the same machine, is built by a second person, and had just generated a real cross-design event.

THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL: build a reflow2 design graph inside storyflow and another inside dynograph-foundation, then have an agent LINK them through their published surfaces and identify where the interfaces are incompatible. WHAT IT WAS MEANT TO PROVE: whether dec:nested-graphs (a graph per ownership boundary) and cap:mirror-surface hold up on designs nobody built to be composed.

=== WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RUN ===
Three real designs, their committed exports, composed against reflow2's live design in a throwaway in-memory graph (nothing written to any of them): reflow2 (1497 nodes, graph_id `reflow2`), dynograph-foundation (179 nodes, graph_id `dynograph-foundation`, export written by reflow2 0.16.0), flo2 (77 nodes, graph_id `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2`, written by 0.24.0). compose_and_analyse then pair_designs, each pair in turn.

=== RESULT 1: THE MECHANISM WORKS ===
Both compositions imported cleanly with ZERO SKIPPED EDGES — 179 nodes / 270 edges from dynograph-foundation, 77 / 181 from flo2. Ids namespaced as designed; neither source design touched.

⭐ CROSS-VERSION COMPOSITION SURVIVED, AND THAT IS A REAL DATA POINT: dynograph-foundation's export was written by reflow2 0.16.0 and imported into a 0.24.0 graph with nothing dropped. [BL-216] filed the three-graphs-three-versions worry on 2026-08-05 as something that "becomes load-bearing the moment cross-graph linking lands". It landed, and it did not bite. That is evidence, not proof — one export, eight minor versions apart, no schema change between them that this design happened to use.

⭐ RESULT 2: A TRUE POSITIVE, AND IT IS THE SEAM THIS WHOLE SESSION WAS ABOUT.
The flo2 pairing reported exactly one CONFLICT: `ifc:core-api` (ours, medium `library`) against `ifc:model-provider-api` (flo2, medium `REST`), names matching at 80/100 — "very likely the same contract, but they cannot be connected as either is currently built." That is precisely the flo2↔reflow2 problem: flo2 is a web app that needs an HTTP surface, reflow2 exposes a library/stdio one, and closing it is what dec:one-process-many-stores and req:reflow2-consumable-as-an-image exist to do. THE TOOL COMPUTED IT FROM TWO DESIGNS NOBODY BUILT TO BE COMPOSED, AND NOBODY TOLD IT THE ANSWER. That is the single strongest piece of evidence this project has that the composition idea is sound.

⚠️ RESULT 3: ZERO PAIRED BOUNDARIES ON BOTH PAIRS, AND THE REASON IS ONE MISSING LABEL.
paired = 0 against dynograph-foundation AND against flo2. seam_findings = 0 on both — which does NOT mean the designs agree; it means NOTHING IS CONNECTED ACROSS THE SEAM. All 15 of dynograph-foundation's published interfaces landed in DEAD SURFACE ("they publish this and nothing here requires it"), and 5 of flo2's did.

THE CAUSE IS SINGULAR: REFLOW2 DECLARES NO `required` INTERFACE ANYWHERE. Pairing matches complements — published/both against required/both, never like with like — so with nothing required, nothing can ever pair. reflow2 compiles against dynograph-core; that dependency is real, load-bearing, already declared in the version manifest (req:design-dependencies-declared, accepted, verified) — AND INVISIBLE TO THE SEAM MACHINERY.

⚠️ THE MOST DANGEROUS NUMBER IN THE RUN IS `unmet_needs: 0`. It reads as "nothing is missing" and it means "we never said we needed anything". A design that has declared no needs cannot have an unmet one. Anyone reading that field without reading `dead_surface: 15` beside it would conclude the seam was healthy.

RELATED, AND THE SAME ROOT: reflow2 holds FIVE Interfaces for 1497 nodes, two of which were created the previous night, and both of those came back as `unclassified_ours` — the tool naming rather than counting them precisely because `internal` is the DEFAULT and cannot distinguish "deliberately internal" from "never classified". This is maturity_report's SEAMS 0 OF 73 appearing as data instead of as a score. A near-miss makes it concrete: dynograph-foundation ALSO publishes an `ifc:core-api`, and reflow2 has one too, and they cannot pair because both are `published` — like-with-like, correctly refused.

⚠️ RESULT 4: TWO FINDINGS THAT BEAR ON THE FEDERATION IDEA RAISED THE SAME DAY.
(1) flo2's graph_id is `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2` while the other two are `reflow2` and `dynograph-foundation` — an opaque mint beside two readable labels. dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs proposes listing graph_ids in a config file; nobody hand-writes `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2` and knows what they typed, so either identity gains a human-facing name or that mechanism needs a different key.
(2) THE ACCESS MODEL ANTHONY DESCRIBED CANNOT BE EXPRESSED IN THE GRAPH AT ALL. He specified: userAJ read/write on all three; userAlex read-only on reflow2, read/write on flo2. `who:ajs` and `who:alex` exist as Contributors and AUTHORED_BY records who DID write something, but there is no node type, edge type or property for who MAY write something. That is not a limitation the trial hit — it is a vocabulary that does not exist, and it is the concrete form of the permission-versus-convenience question left open on dec:idea-need-to-know-compartments.

=== WHAT THIS ANSWERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT ===
ANSWERED: dec:nested-graphs and the composition capabilities hold up on three real designs built at different times by different hands against a moving foundation. Nothing crashed, nothing was silently dropped, the ids namespaced, and the one genuine incompatibility was found and explained in a sentence a person can act on.
NOT ANSWERED, because the run could not reach it: whether seam_report's contract comparison is any good. It needs PAIRS, and there were none. The dependency this decision named — req:interface-spec-complete first, or run against today's thin spec — turns out to have been the wrong dependency: the blocker was not that the spec is thin, it is that nothing is LABELLED as required.

=== THE CHEAPEST NEXT STEP, NOT TAKEN HERE ===
Declare reflow2's `required` interfaces — what it consumes from dynograph-foundation, and what flo2 must be able to reach. A handful of nodes. It would convert 15 dead surfaces into real pairs or real unmet needs, and it is the prerequisite for seam_report ever having anything to compare. Recorded rather than done, because it is design about reflow2's own boundaries and belongs to Anthony's word rather than an agent's tidying.
properties.name: RUN 2026-08-06 — composition proved on reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation: the linking works, the labelling does not exist
properties.rationale:
Anthony's own framing, and it lands on intent reflow2 already holds: req:design-composes (accepted), dec:nested-graphs (DECIDED — a design is its own graph when separately owned, released or shared, which is exactly three sibling repos), cap:mirror-surface and cap:publish-surface (both built). So the LINKING half exists and the COMPARING half does not. Recorded originally as a decision point rather than a plan because the sequencing was a real choice: structure the interface spec first, or run the PoC against today's thin spec to find out what it cannot say.

⭐ THE SEQUENCING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED, AND BOTH BRANCHES WERE WRONG. Running it first was right, and what it found was not "the spec is too thin to compare" — it was that there is nothing to compare, because no boundary on this side is labelled as a need. req:interface-spec-complete was recorded as this PoC's prerequisite; it is not. The prerequisite is a `required` designation on the interfaces reflow2 actually consumes, which is smaller and more specific than making the spec structurally complete.

The second payoff predicted when this was proposed did land: it was the first time reflow2 was pointed at designs it did not author, twice, which is the adopt path Anthony says his real work almost always starts from. The result — clean import, correct namespacing, one true positive, and an honest zero everywhere the design had not been labelled — is the behaviour that path needs.

Kept as `proposed` rather than moved to accepted: the PoC RAN, but what it proposed to prove is only half proven. seam_report was never exercised because pairing produced nothing to feed it, and that half stays open until reflow2 declares what it requires. Recorded via chg:linked-repos-trial-run.
